newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank crown policy sound for now - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank crown policy sound for now - dealers.

text.p: The Slovak central bank is right to assume that there will be no imminent attack on the crown but ever more restrictive adminstrative measures are unsustainable in the longer term, dealers said on Friday.

National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) vice governor Marian Jusko told Friday's Narodna Obroda daily that foreign speculators stood to lose money if they attacked the crown and that the currency would be stable at current levels.
"They can keep the Slovak crown steady in the short and medium term," Tibor Frantik of ING Bank told Reuters.
"It's what I thought they (the NBS) were thinking...it's a confirmation. The vice governor told us that they are adding liquidity not at a huge pace...that's really good I think," he added.
The NBS has been gradually adding small amounts of liquidity to the crown market which is 37 percent short of minimum reserve requirements, according to the latest NBS figures.

But in an effort to avoid the fate suffered by the Czech crown, which lost nearly 10 percent of its value after a sustained speculative assault, the NBS has deliberately kept liquidity on the interbank market low. It has also intervened directly to support the crown.

The measures have held the crown at around minus 0.6 percent against the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket but the lack of liquidity, has pushed interbank money market rates to extraordinary levels.
On Friday, average overnight interbank rates were quoted at 30 percent on the bid and 80 percent on the offer side.
"In the long run there is no choice to keep it like this unless we want to build a fence around the whole country," said one trader for a foreign bank based in Bratislava.
Even the largest Slovak companies often use short-term crown loans to help refinance their activities.
"Tell me what sort of business can afford to borrow money at 50, or 100 percent?" he asked.

In a sign of the central bank's determination to further strengthen its support for the crown, the NBS said on Wednesday it would soon begin monitoring bank positions on a daily rather than a 10-day basis.
The same dealer, who requested anonymity, said the new policy could herald an even tighter regime of adminstrative measures against speculators. He had no details.
